claim: Storing activations in int8 during the forward pass and dequantizing them for the backward pass cuts Transformer training memory by roughly half at equal or slightly better accuracy, so activation precision is a real lever on a per-card memory ceiling.
stance_target: The repo's premise that per-card memory, not compute, is the binding constraint for a 7B-total model on 64 GB cards
scope_conditions: Vision Transformers (DeiT, Swin, PVT) trained on ImageNet / CIFAR-100 / ADE20K with PyTorch or CUDA implementations of Mesa; no LLM or long-context experiments
quoted_support: on DeiT-B and Swin-Ti, Mesa achieves the same performance as the baselines while reducing the memory footprint by 51% and 55%, respectively.

claim: The memory saving is paid for in throughput: compressing the whole model halves single-GPU training speed, and DeiT-Ti falls from 1,196 to 431 images/s at 2,000 MB versus 4,149 MB baseline.
stance_target: The idea that activation quantization is a free memory win on a compute-limited box
scope_conditions: Single-GPU measurements, DeiT-Ti, PyTorch implementation, running-estimates variant
quoted_support: In an extreme case, Mesa could result in the throughput decreases by half on a single GPU when compressing a whole model.

claim: On a slow interconnect the activation-quantization throughput penalty is largely hidden, because communication rather than compute dominates step time; Mesa costs only 15% extra GPU hours for PVT-Ti in distributed training.
stance_target: The repo's claim that on a 0.75 GiB/s fabric, compute-side overheads can be absorbed behind communication
scope_conditions: Distributed multi-GPU training of PVT-Ti and DeiT-Ti; the paper's own clusters are NVLink-class, so the hiding effect should be stronger on PCIe Gen2 x4
quoted_support: although the throughput on a single GPU is reduced by using Mesa, the total training time on ImageNet is similar to that of baseline DeiT-Ti as the communication overheads have more impact on the training speed under the distributed training scheme.
numbers: similar total ImageNet training time to baseline

claim: Head-wise quantization is necessary because multi-head self-attention activations have heterogeneous distributions across heads, so per-tensor clipping ranges are too coarse.
stance_target: Whether a generic activation-quantization implementation transfers to a new architecture without per-head calibration
scope_conditions: MSA layers of DeiT/Swin/PVT; head-wise grouping of activations for clipping ranges and offsets
quoted_support: we identify the heterogeneous activation distributions in an MSA layer of a Transformer. For this, we proposed a head-wise activation quantization strategy, which groups the activations based on each self-attention head to capture better quantization clipping ranges and offsets.

claim: Memory saved by activation quantization can be reinvested as a larger batch under the same memory budget: DeiT-Ti at total batch 2,048 uses 33.4 GB versus 28.8 GB for mixed precision at batch 1,024, and gains 0.8% Top-1.
stance_target: The repo's strategy of buying global batch size with memory savings rather than adding GPUs
scope_conditions: 8x NVIDIA V100, ImageNet, DeiT-Ti and Swin-S
quoted_support: training DeiT-Ti with the default strategy requires at least 34GB GPU memory under a total batch size of 1,024. However, with the same memory budget, we can double the batch size to better utilise available GPU cores and explore potential benefits of using larger batch size.

claim: Nearest rounding is not sufficient for activation quantization: DeiT-Ti with nearest rounding fails to converge on ImageNet, so stochastic rounding is required for correctness.
stance_target: Any plan to quantize activations with a naive cast (round-to-nearest) to save memory
scope_conditions: DeiT-Ti, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet, Mesa with nearest rounding versus stochastic rounding
quoted_support: although training DeiT-Ti with nearest rounding can achieve competitive results on CIFAR-100, it fails to converge on ImageNet. Therefore, we speculate that stochastic rounding is important to guarantee good performance in Mesa.

claim: Compressing only part of the model gives a tunable memory-speed tradeoff: MSA layers alone save 27% memory, FFN layers alone 21%, and compressing both gives the most memory at the slowest speed.
stance_target: Whether a partial activation-quantization policy can hit a specific 64 GB budget without paying the full throughput cost
scope_conditions: DeiT-Ti on CIFAR-100, per-module compression ablation
quoted_support: compressing the MSA or FFN layers in DeiT-Ti can reduce 27% and 21% memory footprint at training time, respectively.

claim: The evidence base is vision-only: all results are on ImageNet, CIFAR-100 and ADE20K, with no language model or long-context run, so the 32k-activation-memory case the repo cares about is untested by this paper.
stance_target: Whether Mesa-style activation quantization can be assumed to work for a 32k-context LLM step on this box
scope_conditions: Scope limitation of the paper's own evaluation suite
quoted_support: Extensive experiments on ImageNet, CIFAR-100 and ADE20K demonstrate that Mesa can achieve flexible memory-savings (up to 50%) during training while achieving comparable or even better performance.

claim: Activation storage, not weights, is what makes long-sequence Transformer training memory-intensive, which is the mechanism that binds a 32k-context step.
stance_target: The repo's claim that activations at 32k with checkpointing are the dominant per-card memory term
quoted_support: training such networks is extremely memory intensive owing to storing all intermediate activations that are needed for gradient computation during backpropagation, especially for long sequences.

claim: Approximated activations can act as a regularizer, which is the paper's explanation for accuracy sometimes exceeding the exact-activation baseline.
stance_target: Whether quantization noise in activations is harmful or benign at small scale
scope_conditions: DeiT-Ti/S on ImageNet and CIFAR-100, authors' conjecture rather than an isolated experiment
quoted_support: Our conjecture is that the approximated activations help to regularize the stochastic gradients when training Transformers, which therefore improves the model performance.
